title: How one creator built two games with AI in about 80 hours each. The hard part was boss fights.
author: pavelbains
selftext:
I run Cipher, the platform these two games are published on, so factor that in.

[Tachimi](https://gocipher.gg/creators/tachimi) built ROTBORN, a dark 2D action platformer, and Black Ledger, a top-down action shooter. Each took about 80 hours to get where it is now. That covers the assets, the combat system, and refining animations and boss fights through playtesting. His own estimate for doing this the traditional way is 3,500+ hours.  
  
[https://gocipher.gg/games/rotborn](https://gocipher.gg/games/rotborn)  
[https://gocipher.gg/games/black-ledger](https://gocipher.gg/games/black-ledger)

His workflow was a tight loop: describe a change, test it in the game, keep refining. He says that loop is what kept the project moving, especially on combat, where a small change to timing or effects can change how a fight feels. 

The hard part was the bosses. Getting attack timing, warning cues, and visual effects to work together took the most iteration. His goal was a fight that feels intense but where you can still read the attack and react. The core atmosphere matched what he pictured from the start. The details, mainly boss mechanics and how attacks signal danger, only came out of playtesting.

The games run on Cipher's own engine. He used the Cipher Editor and built locally with Cipher's CLI. Assets, code, and animation were generated through Cipher.

For those building with AI: what part of game dev do the tools still handle badly, and what would you want them to do for you?
